1. Load the spotify dataset (available in github repository).
```{r}
library(readr)
spotifyDat <- read_csv("C:/Users/xxiny/Downloads/spotifyDat Fall26.csv")
View(spotifyDat)
```

2. Create a bar graph of the artist column (Hint: use theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90)) to rotate the x axis).
```{r}
library(ggplot2)
ggplot(spotifyDat, aes(artist)) + geom_bar() + labs(y = "Number of Songs") + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90)) + theme(text = element_text(size = 6)) 
```

3. Add genre as a third variable in your graph.
```{r}
ggplot(spotifyDat, aes(artist, fill = genre), ) + geom_bar() + labs(y = "Number of Songs") + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90)) + theme(text = element_text(size = 6)) 
```

4. Use color brewer to add color to your graph in 3. 
```{r}
ggplot(spotifyDat, aes(artist, fill = genre), ) + geom_bar() + labs(y = "Number of Songs") + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90)) + theme(text = element_text(size = 6)) + scale_fill_brewer("Purples")
```

5. Place the legend for the graph you made in 3 on the bottom of the graph. 
```{r}
ggplot(spotifyDat, aes(artist, fill = genre), ) + geom_bar() + labs(y = "Number of Songs") + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90)) + theme(text = element_text(size = 6)) + theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

As you probably recognized, the graph you made is really hard to read.

6. Separate the genre column into multiple columns (e.g. so each genre listed is in a unique column)
```{r}
library(tidyverse)
spotifyDat <- spotifyDat |> separate(genre, into = c("genre1", "genre2", "genre3", "genre4"), sep = ", ")
```

7. Use these genre columns to create a dataset in long format. 
```{r}
spotifyLong <- spotifyDat |> pivot_longer(cols = c("genre1", "genre2", "genre3", "genre4"), names_to = "genreNum", values_to = "songGenre", values_drop_na = TRUE)
```

8.use facet wrap to make graphs of artist by genre 
```{r}
class(spotifyLong$songGenre)
spotifyLong$songGenre <- as.factor(spotifyLong$songGenre)
levels(spotifyLong$songGenre)

spotifyLong$artist <- as.factor(spotifyLong$artist)
levels(spotifyLong$artist)

spotifyLong <- spotifyLong |> filter(songGenre != "set()")

#faceted bar graph including all artists and song genre
ggplot(spotifyLong, aes(artist)) + geom_bar() + facet_wrap(~songGenre) + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90)) + theme(text = element_text(size = 6))

```
```{r}

summary(spotifyLong)

#keeping only 6 artists with most songs and get rid of set() song genre so that the graph is more readable
spotifyLong1 <- spotifyLong |> filter(artist == "Rihanna" | artist == "Drake" | artist == "Calvin Harris" | artist == "David Guetta" | artist == "Chris Brown" | artist == "Nelly") 

ggplot(spotifyLong1, aes(artist)) + geom_bar() + facet_wrap(~songGenre) + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90))
```



9. Create a graph that includes the variables tempo and dancability. 
```{r}
ggplot(spotifyLong, aes(tempo, danceability)) + geom_point() + facet_wrap(~songGenre)

```

  
10. Add popularity as a third variable. 
```{r}
ggplot(spotifyLong, aes(tempo, danceability, color = popularity)) + geom_point() + facet_wrap(~songGenre)

```

11. Use viridis as a color in your graph from #10
```{r}
library(viridis)
ggplot(spotifyLong, aes(tempo, danceability, color = popularity)) + geom_point() + facet_wrap(~songGenre) + scale_color_viridis(discrete = "FALSE", option = "magma")
```
